summary.text: Ben Ray Luján is the Democratic incumbent U.S. Senator from New Mexico, first elected in 2020. He grew up in Nambé, worked in state government, served on the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (2004-2008), and represented New Mexico's 3rd Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2009 to 2021, including a term as House Assistant Speaker. He is seeking a second Senate term.

paragraphs.text: Luján was born in Santa Fe, New Mexico, in 1972 and grew up in Nambé, a small farming community north of Santa Fe. His father, Ben Luján, was a longtime member of the New Mexico House of Representatives and its speaker, and his Senate biography says he is a Head Start graduate.
He graduated from Pojoaque Valley High School in 1990 and earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from New Mexico Highlands University in 2007.
Before entering elected office, Luján worked as director of administrative services and chief financial officer of the New Mexico Cultural Affairs Department.

He served on the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission from 2004 to 2008 and chaired it. His Senate biography says he worked with colleagues to develop a renewable portfolio standard for New Mexico utilities.
Luján won the 3rd Congressional District seat in 2008, succeeding Tom Udall, and served in the U.S. House from 2009 to 2021.

House Minority Leader Nancy Pelosi chose him in November 2014 to chair the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, making him the first Latino selected as either party's campaign chairman. House Democrats elected him assistant majority leader for the 116th Congress, a post his Senate biography calls House Assistant Speaker.

In 2020 Luján defeated Republican Mark Ronchetti, 51.7% to 45.6%, for the U.S. Senate seat Udall had held, and he has served in the Senate since January 2021. He sits on the Commerce, Science, and Transportation; Finance; Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry; Indian Affairs; and Budget committees.
He suffered a serious stroke in 2022 that required hospitalization and surgery; he has since recovered and has advocated for stroke prevention and treatment efforts.

According to his Senate website, he received the James Beard Impact Award in June 2026 for his work to restore the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), and he has led efforts to strengthen the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act program.
